stem: Which of the following is the preferred modern management for a lateral cervical lymphatic malformation (cystic hygroma) to minimize morbidity?

options.text: Formal surgical excision with wide margins.
Image-guided sclerotherapy using agents like Bleomycin or $OK432$.
Observation and monitoring for spontaneous resolution during puberty.
A prolonged course of broad-spectrum oral antibiotics.

explanation: Sclerotherapy induces an inflammatory response that causes the lesion to shrink, avoiding the complications of major surgery.
rationale: Think about the interventional radiology techniques mentioned as being less invasive than surgery.

optionExplanations.A: Surgical excision is often more morbid due to the risk of damaging surrounding nerves and vessels compared to minimally invasive options.
optionExplanations.B: Sclerotherapy induces an inflammatory response that causes the lesion to shrink, avoiding the complications of major surgery.
optionExplanations.C: While some lesions are monitored, active intervention is usually required if they are symptomatic or enlarging, and they rarely resolve completely on their own.
optionExplanations.D: Antibiotics treat secondary bacterial infections but do not address the underlying anatomical malformation of the lymphatic system.
